chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Alawi, all from al-Fatah ibn Yazid al-Jurjani, who said:

The road brought me together with Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) during my return from Mecca to Khurasan, while he was travelling to Iraq. I heard him saying: 'Whoever fears God will be feared, and whoever obeys God will be obeyed.'

So I approached him subtly, arrived, greeted him, and he returned my greeting. Then he said: 'O Fatah! Whoever pleases the Creator will not care about the anger of the creatures, and whoever angers the Creator deserves that God unleash the anger of the creatures upon him.'

And indeed the Creator cannot be described except by what He Himself has described Himself with — and how can One be described Whom the senses are unable to perceive, imaginations unable to grasp, passing thoughts unable to delimit, and visions unable to encompass? He is more Majestic than what the describers describe Him as, and more Exalted than what the characterisers characterise.

He is distant in His closeness and near in His distance — so in His distance He is near, and in His closeness He is far. He established the 'how', so one cannot ask 'how'; and He established the 'where', so one cannot ask 'where' — for He transcends how-ness and where-ness.

key_terms.الأينونية: Where-ness / locality — the philosophical category of place or location, which is inapplicable to God
key_terms.التقوى: Taqwa — God-consciousness, piety; the quality of fearing God that protects one from fearing creation
key_terms.الخالق: The Creator — a Divine name emphasising God's creative sovereignty over all existence
key_terms.الكيفوفية: How-ness / modality — the philosophical category of quality or manner, which cannot be predicated of God
key_terms.سخط المخلوق: The wrath of the creature — the anger of created beings, which holds no ultimate power over one who has earned God's pleasure

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about pleasing God versus fearing creation?
ai.summary: This hadith records a chance encounter between al-Fatah ibn Yazid al-Jurjani and Imam al-Ridha (AS) during a journey from Mecca. The Imam teaches a profound two-part lesson: first, the practical principle that pleasing God immunises one against human opposition, and angering God invites it; second, a sophisticated apophatic theology asserting that God transcends all categories of human thought — sense-perception, imagination, fleeting notions, and vision — and that questions of 'how' and 'where' are inapplicable to the Divine. The encounter illustrates the Imam's role as a living teacher accessible on the road, and the theology reflects classical Shia kalami emphasis on Divine transcendence (tanzih).
